messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Feb 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment boundaries & migration intent — quick recap + asks

Hi Kyle / Lydia,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and clear priorities. Below is a short recap plus three quick asks so we can size a pilot and recommend the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary goal: move chat + triage pipeline into a production inference platform with predictable latency and cost.
- Data sensitivity: we need to separate PHI-containing flows (claims processing) from low-risk user-facing chat.
- Current mix: OpenAI API for prototyping + internal PyTorch GPU cluster for nightly batch jobs.
- Key constraints: latency for real-time chat (~200ms p50 target), KV-cache warmup for session continuity, and procurement window (Q2 budget).

Three asks (please reply inline):
1) Hosting preference for pilot — choose one: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserving GPU pools), or Private VPC / on-prem (PHI needs).
2) Migration origin — which traffic will we move first? (a) OpenAI API requests, (b) self-hosted PyTorch cluster (batch), (c) legacy GPU cluster serving inference.
3) Target timeline for a production cutover (target month or number of weeks).

I attached a short migration-summary spreadsheet that maps the above (atlas_migration_summary.xlsx). If you can answer the three asks this week we’ll put together a pilot scope and cost estimate for ~100k requests/day.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up next Wed (2/28) to review the pilot scope and pricing. If that works for you I’ll send an invite.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@atlashealth.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment boundaries & migration intent — quick recap + asks

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. Answering inline below.

1) Hosting preference for pilot:
- We want to pilot on Dedicated capacity first. The primary driver is predictable throughput and the ability to reserve capacity for peak hours.
- For PHI flows, we are evaluating Private VPC; we may require a VPC proof-of-concept before production for that subset.

2) Migration origin:
- Phase 1: Move the OpenAI API traffic (chat feature) to Redwood Dedicated.
- Phase 2: Rework batch jobs that currently run on our PyTorch cluster — these can stay on self-hosted for now, but we want an integration plan.
- Legacy GPU cluster: low priority, we may decommission after we stabilize on Dedicated.

3) Timeline:
- Pilot start: mid-March (around 3/15) if procurement goes smoothly.
- Production cutover for non-PHI chat: targeted by end of Q2.

Other notes / constraints:
- KV cache: our stateful session cache lives in Redis; we need guidance on keeping session continuity during cutover and a way to warm caches in Redwood.
- Latency: our p50 target is ~200ms; p95 under 600ms.
- Compliance: any Private/VPC path must integrate with our KMS (AWS KMS) and show audit logs for inference requests.

Kyle
Kyle Morgan
Director of AI Platforms | Atlas Health

Subject: Pilot proposal: Dedicated + Private PoC for PHI — timeline & next steps

Kyle / Lydia — thanks for the fast answers and the timeline. Based on your constraints I propose the following minimal plan so procurement can review a single recommended path:

Recommended approach (two-track):
- Track A (Pilot — Recommended): Redwood Dedicated capacity for non-PHI chat traffic. Benefits: fastest time-to-value, predictable throughput, no changes to your app layer for initial cutover.
- Track B (PHI PoC): Private VPC proof-of-concept for PHI-containing flows — we’ll do an isolated deployment integrated with your AWS KMS and audit log collection. If PoC checks boxes, we’ll propose a phased migration to Private for PHI only.

High-level timeline (approx):
- Week 0 (procurement signoff): contract + SOW (1 week).
- Weeks 1–3 (Pilot setup): Dedicated capacity reserved, credentials & test traffic, KV-cache warmers configured, load tests.
- Weeks 2–6 (PHI PoC): Private VPC provisioning, KMS integration, sample PHI dataset verification, audit log validation.
- Post-PoC: Rollout plan for production cutover (sync plan for Redis sessions, rollout by traffic slice).

Migration runbook highlights:
- Data sync: snapshot current Redis session store; start redirecting a small % of traffic to Dedicated while keeping origin reads as fallback.
- KV-cache warmers: run a warm-up job in Dedicated using recent session keys; verify tokenization/embedding parity on a sample corpus.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing back to OpenAI/self-hosted if p95 latency or error rate spike above agreed SLO.

Estimated next steps I’ll send this afternoon: pricing for 100k req/day on Dedicated, cost delta for Private PoC, and a short playbook PDF. Proposed follow-up: Thu 2/29 11:00 AM ET — 30 minutes to walk the pilot SOW. If that slot doesn't work, give two alternatives.
